evidence.quote: McConnelsville is located on the east bank of the Muskingum River, opposite Malta. There are two bridges across the river, on 3rd and 7th streets, the latter forming part of State Route 78.

evidence.claim: The Morgan County Scenic Byway runs through the Appalachian foothills, with a crossing of the Muskingum between Malta and McConnelsville.
evidence.quote: The foothills of the Appalachian Mountains are a perfect setting for this byway

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration highlights covered and iron bridges, wildlife areas, historic districts and state parks as its attractions, and allows an hour for the drive.
evidence.quote: Time to Allow Allow 1 hour. Fees None The foothills of the Appalachian Mountains are a perfect setting for this byway s rustic beauty. It s rustic beauty is embodied in its covered and iron bridges, wildlife areas, historic districts, and state parks.

evidence.claim: Before that road crossing, the river became a major route for transport and trade after locks and dams were built between 1836 and 1841.
evidence.quote: the Muskingum River, which became a significant transportation and trade route after the construction of a system of locks and dams between 1836 and 1841.

evidence.claim: Malta grew through the nineteenth century because of its position on the river.
evidence.quote: The village developed throughout the 19th century due to its strategic location on the Muskingum River

evidence.claim: The 1913 Morgan County Veterans’ Memorial Bridge later linked Malta and McConnelsville and became part of the Muskingum River Navigation Historic District.
evidence.quote: Morgan County Veterans' Memorial Bridge -- built in 1913, the bridge spans the Muskingum River between Malta and McConnelsville and is part of the Muskingum River Navigation Historic District.

evidence.claim: Begin at Bishopville on State Route 78, beside the southern edge of Burr Oak State Park.
evidence.quote: Bishopville is located on Ohio State Route 78, 2 miles (3 km) east of Glouster. The community is nestled on the south side of Burr Oak State Park

evidence.claim: The road reaches Ringgold at the junction with Route 555, southwest of Malta.
evidence.quote: Ringgold is located at the junction of State Routes 78 and 555, 7.5 miles (12.1 km) southwest of Malta.

evidence.claim: Malta occupies the west bank of the Muskingum; across the river, Route 78 enters McConnelsville on the 7th Street bridge.
evidence.quote: McConnelsville is located on the east bank of the Muskingum River, opposite Malta. There are two bridges across the river, on 3rd and 7th streets, the latter forming part of State Route 78.

evidence.claim: with a crossing of the Muskingum between Malta and McConnelsville.
evidence.quote: McConnelsville is located on the east bank of the Muskingum River, opposite Malta. There are two bridges across the river, on 3rd and 7th streets, the latter forming part of State Route 78.

evidence.claim: Bishopville stands on State Route 78 along the south side of Burr Oak State Park.
evidence.quote: Bishopville is located on Ohio State Route 78, 2 miles (3 km) east of Glouster. The community is nestled on the south side of Burr Oak State Park

evidence.claim: James M. Bishop laid out the community in 1859 and gave it his name.
evidence.quote: Bishopville was laid out in 1859 by James M. Bishop, and named for him.

evidence.claim: The neighboring lake came much later: the Army Corps of Engineers began Tom Jenkins Dam in March 1948 and completed it in February 1950.
evidence.quote: Construction began under the Army Corps of Engineers in March 1948 and was completed in February 1950.

evidence.claim: The earth-fill dam was built for flood control, recreation and drinking water for the Athens area.
evidence.quote: The Tom Jenkins Dam is a rolled-earth fill structure constructed to control flooding, provide recreation, as well as drinking water for the Athens, Ohio area.

evidence.claim: Burr Oak State Park was dedicated in 1952.
evidence.quote: The park was dedicated in 1952.

evidence.claim: The Morgan County Dungeon is a small stone jail preserved on Malta’s Main Street.
evidence.quote: The dungeon was rediscovered during construction in 1964 and later relocated and preserved on Main Street.

evidence.claim: It measures approximately 11 feet long, 5 feet wide and 12 feet high.
evidence.quote: Measuring approximately 11 feet long, 5 feet wide, and 12 feet high,

evidence.claim: People convicted of larceny, rioting and adultery were confined inside.
evidence.quote: it was used to confine individuals convicted of crimes such as larceny, rioting, and adultery.

evidence.claim: Construction work uncovered the jail in 1964; it was subsequently moved to Main Street, where an Ohio Historical Marker identifies it.
evidence.quote: The dungeon was rediscovered during construction in 1964 and later relocated and preserved on Main Street. It is now marked by an Ohio Historical Marker.

evidence.claim: Its construction is believed to date to the 1830s.
evidence.quote: a small stone jail believed to have been built in the 1830s.

evidence.claim: Electric light was an early distinction of McConnelsville’s opera house, built in 1892 on the northwest corner of the public square.
evidence.quote: Opera House -- located on the northwest corner of the public square, the building was built in 1892 and was one of the first buildings in the county to be lit by electric light.

evidence.claim: It was among the first buildings in Morgan County to use it.
evidence.quote: was one of the first buildings in the county to be lit by electric light.

evidence.claim: The stage hosted traveling shows and speakers including William Jennings Bryan, Reverend Billy Sunday and Senator Albert Beveridge.
evidence.quote: A variety of productions, traveling shows, performers, and celebrities have appeared in the Opera House: Reverend Billy Sunday, William Jennings Bryan, and Senator Albert Beveridge spoke there.

evidence.claim: Downtown also has the Greek Revival courthouse, designed by William P. Johnson and built in 1858.
evidence.quote: Morgan County Courthouse -- located in downtown McConnelsville, the Greek Revival style building was designed by architect William P. Johnson and built in 1858

evidence.claim: The Muskingum separates Malta on the west bank from McConnelsville on the east.
evidence.quote: McConnelsville is located on the east bank of the Muskingum River, opposite Malta.

evidence.claim: The Muskingum separates Malta on the west bank from McConnelsville on the east.
evidence.quote: Malta is located on the west side of the Muskingum River, opposite McConnelsville.

evidence.claim: An Ohio Historical Marker identifies the relocated stone jail on Main Street.
evidence.quote: The dungeon was rediscovered during construction in 1964 and later relocated and preserved on Main Street. It is now marked by an Ohio Historical Marker.

evidence.claim: The lake covers 664 acres; the park borders Wayne National Forest and Sunday Creek State Wildlife Area.
evidence.quote: The area of the park is 2,593 acres (1,049 ha), while that of the lake is 664 acres (269 ha). The park was dedicated in 1952. The park borders the Wayne National Forest and the Sunday Creek State Wildlife Area.

evidence.claim: The courthouse houses the Court of Common Pleas and its probate and juvenile divisions in the building completed for $10,000.
evidence.quote: built in 1858 at a cost of $10,000. The building is still in use and today, housing the Morgan County Court of Common Pleas and its probate and juvenile divisions.

evidence.claim: McConnelsville is Morgan County’s seat.
evidence.quote: McConnelsville is a village in and the county seat of Morgan County, Ohio

flags: Cache gives little road geometry, no construction or campaigning history, and no explicit state designation record. Overview uses the FHWA byway description and river-crossing history, and remains shorter than 200 words.

FHWA gives 39 miles; material maps 31.8. Omitted length. Cache does not establish the precise east endpoint or the Route 78 link to Meigs, so the driving narrative stops at the last supported crossing rather than inventing an endpoint.
Dropped current claim that both river towns grew because of the locks and dams: the cache explicitly establishes that connection only for Malta.
The 1913 historic bridge and Route 78’s 7th Street bridge are not equated; cache does not establish they are the same structure.
The jail’s dimensions and construction date retain source qualifications. Short Malta moment avoids adding unverified details.
Current has no motifs fields; story motifs is empty and retained moments preserve absent motifs. No site hours or interior access are asserted.
Bishopville public dock is supported by its cache page but omitted because no site-manager access page was supplied; no claim of present dock access is made.
